classification.difficultyReason: Reframe a common remainder of 1 as a common multiple after subtracting 1, then use the LCM to establish the smallest permitted number.

content.prompt: Write down the smallest whole number greater than 1 which leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by:

answer.worked:
Subtracting 1 gives a common multiple. Use the largest power of each prime factor to find the LCM.
$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{LCM}(2,3,5)&=2\times3\times5\\\operatorname{LCM}(2,3,5)&=30\\30+1&=31\end{align*}$$

Subtracting 1 gives a common multiple. Use the largest power of each prime factor to find the LCM.
$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{LCM}(2,3,7)&=2\times3\times7\\\operatorname{LCM}(2,3,7)&=42\\42+1&=43\end{align*}$$

Subtracting 1 gives a common multiple. Since $9=3^2$, use the largest power of each prime factor.
$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{LCM}(2,5,9)&=2\times3^2\times5\\\operatorname{LCM}(2,5,9)&=90\\90+1&=91\end{align*}$$

Subtracting 1 gives a common multiple. Since $4=2^2$, use the largest power of each prime factor.
$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{LCM}(2,3,4)&=2^2\times3\\\operatorname{LCM}(2,3,4)&=12\\12+1&=13\end{align*}$$

Subtracting 1 gives a common multiple. Since $12=2^2\times3$, use the largest power of each prime factor.
$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{LCM}(3,5,12)&=2^2\times3\times5\\\operatorname{LCM}(3,5,12)&=60\\60+1&=61\end{align*}$$

Subtracting 1 gives a common multiple. Since $4=2^2$ and $9=3^2$, use the largest power of each prime factor.
$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{LCM}(2,3,4,9)&=2^2\times3^2\\\operatorname{LCM}(2,3,4,9)&=36\\36+1&=37\end{align*}$$
